name: Gloria Sloan
life: “I still remember taking a shop picture reflected in a puddle.” On Wednesday, near Breakwater Way, Gloria stops on the landward side of the cycle track to watch the first boats turn for home.
voice: I took the photo everyone liked. The man in the front doesn't want his face online and I'm collecting the copies.
appearance: Gloria has short sandy hair and a marked widow's peak, a broad nose and a deep dimple on one cheek, and a favorite piece of clothing, an old plum windbreaker. It usually goes with a pen clipped inside the neckline. When somebody else has the floor, Gloria counts on the side of one finger where hardly anybody notices.
personality: Gloria carries anger into a conversation very slowly. Once it arrives, a quiet statement of facts can be considerably harder to sidestep than a shout.
agenda: To withdraw unauthorized copies of the open-day picture.
family: Sofia Brady is Gloria’s cousin raised in the same household. Gloria chooses an ordinary story to tell. Sofia asks the question the rest of the family avoided. They tend to get further with an important subject when it arrives in the middle of talk about dinner or work. Asked about *An empty dedication*, Sofia says, “I held the author's baby every Thursday. I was paid and I'm proud of the work that payment bought.”
connections: Frank Moran. A warm drink at the gathering becomes a reason to ask before publishing the photograph.

reactions.response: Gloria records the petitioners who are present and asks them how to recover the others.

reactions.situation: Somebody says a missing friend must be avoiding their calls
reactions.response: Gloria asks what the friend actually said last time and checks whether anybody is expecting them at home.

reactions.response: Gloria offers to accompany them while they tell the truth.
